messages:
Marisol: quick follow-up from today's all-hands — a handful of infra/capacity Qs landed in the chat about APAC GPUs and autoscale behavior. dropping them here so leadership + infra can respond.

Priya: can we get a clear ETA for APAC GPU availability (reserved + hosted)? and are we planning pre-warmed pools in region or relying on cross-region burst? :thinking_face: 

Liam: also curious how autoscaler will prioritize capacity when supply is tight — e.g., dedicated customers vs. hosted best-effort traffic vs. internal infra jobs. any chance we can get a short priority table?

Sam: small ops question — will fallbacks be automatic model-variants or forced routing to other regions? what's the expected client-visible behavior?

Jesse: short answers to unblock folks: 1) APAC supply ETA — we're targeting an initial soft availability window in November 2025 for reserved pools (pilot customers), with GA for hosted/standard reservations by Jan 2026. this is contingent on a couple of outstanding hardware contracts but procurement + partners look healthy. 2) warm pools — yes for Dedicated/reserved SKUs only; Hosted will use routing + burst buffers, not full warm pools due to cost. 3) priority — Dedicated (SLA-backed) > Reserved long-term commitments > Hosted on best-effort; internal infra jobs run in a separate quota band and won't steal customer capacity.

Marisol: thanks Jesse — can you confirm whether warm pools are per-region or global? we heard mixed signals in the AMA.

Jesse: warm pools are regionally scoped. we will seed APAC warm pools once we hit the pilot inventory milestone so cold-starts are rare for Dedicated customers. Hosted fallthrough will prefer intra-region, then nearest healthy region, then model-fallback.

Liam: technical detail — autoscaler behavior we plan: keep warm_pool_size = 10% of committed capacity for Dedicated in-region. when demand spikes above buffer, autoscaler will: 1) burst within region if spare GPUs exist, 2) route to near region (latency-aware), 3) if latency budget exceeded, degrade to fallback model variant. we'll publish the P95/P99 SLOs per step.

Priya: example config snippet for the autoscaler we've been testing:
```
policy:
  warm_pool: 0.10  # fraction of committed nodes to keep warm
  burst_multiplier: 1.4
  routing_preference: [region, nearest, fallback_model]
  fallback_models: ["rwd-llm-8q", "rwd-llm-4q"]
```

Marisol: what about preemption? if a preemptible pool is used for burst, will we transparently retry on a non-preemptible node?

Liam: yes — burst capacity can include preemptible instances; requests on preemptible nodes get a retry/handoff window of 90s before falling back to another lane. we favor fast retries over immediate client errors.

Sam: customers asked about SLA language — will Dedicated contracts explicitly call out warm-pool guarantees?

Jesse: yes, Dedicated SKUs will have explicit warm-pool sizing and a latency uptime commitment. Hosted SLAs will be more availability/cost-targeted and will reference our routing fallback behavior. legal and sales to add exact wording into the contract templates.

Priya: action items i heard — publish APAC timeline doc + pilot criteria (Marisol), update autoscaler runbook & public-facing section on fallback behavior (Liam), add SLA paragraph for warm pools to dedicated contract template (Jesse/Sales). will follow up with owners here.

Marisol: OPS-OWNERS: i'll own the APAC timeline doc. will post draft tomorrow and link to infra roadmap.

Liam: i'll update the autoscaler runbook and put a short explainer in the public docs about the multi-step fallback.

Jesse: i'll coordinate contract language with sales/legal and ping here once ready.

ops-bot: Reminder — canary rollout for APAC warm-pools scheduled: 2025-10-15 03:00 UTC -> 2025-10-22 03:00 UTC. See deploy dashboard: https://deploy.redwood.example/canaries/2025-apac-warm-pool

Sam: thanks all. if anyone wants me to surface a short FAQ for customers re: what they can expect during pilot vs GA, i can draft it for PM channel. :+1:

Marisol: please do, Sam. putting follow-ups as comments in the roadmap doc so we keep a single source of truth. :white_check_mark:

Priya: thanks team — this helps a lot. i'll update the thread when the runbook PR lands.

Jesse: appreciate the quick sync. we'll keep updates frequent while these milestones approach.
